problems.claim_category: False uniqueness characterization in a main theorem
problems.source_locator: p.4 Theorem 1.4, equation (1.8); p.36 first paragraph of Section 5
problems.hypotheses: 4<kappa<8; a>0; real x<1-kappa/8; analytic continuation of moment formulas where needed
problems.decisive_evidence: For kappa=6,a=1, x=-1/12 and x=5/48 both satisfy the raw sine equation and are below1/4. Radicands0 and9. The first cannot be a probability exponent at a=1.
problems.counterevidence: Equation (1.9) gives5/48. Theorem1.3's filled sine ratio yields a strictly increasing moment, hence a unique intended root.
problems.core_dependency: Definition of Root(a), identification Lambda(Root(a))=-log(aP(Tc)), and Theorem1.4 characterization.
problems.repair: Use a E[R^(-x)1_Tc]=1 with removable limit, or sinc(u)=a r sinc(r u). x0 is retained exactly at a=1/r.
problems.impact_boundary: Existence of the exponent, closed forms, and the intended moment root are not disproved.

problems.counterevidence: Preceding sentence calls a^2 a variance, suggesting omitted factors on diagonal. Replacing both diagonal entries by a^2 t gives determinant4t^2>0.

problems.repair: Specify one consistent covariance/time normalization; audit inherited excursion and quantum-area constants.
problems.impact_boundary: Local impossibility proved; final welding and moment theorems not disproved. No all-constant audit claimed.
